files.html: //! examples/audio_scale_star_hands - a scale played with two hands: the left hand chooses a chord, the right hand plays //! its notes. One scale - a tonic and a mode, C Ionian to begin with - is shown several ways at once, and every view //! lights the same notes as they sound, in the same colors: each degree of the scale has its color in every key, the //! tonic red, so that what a note does in the key, not which note it is, is what the eye learns. //! //! The window //! //! +---------+----------------------------------------+---------+ //! | options | [ I ] [ V ] [ vi ] [ IV ] editor | the | //! +---------+ | twelve | //! | key's | | notes | //! | window | the star +---------+ //! | | | what | //! +---------+ | sounds | //! | chooser | | | //! +---------+----------------------------------------+---------+ //! | keyboard | [ ] | //! +------------------------------------------------------+-----+ //! //! the editor the progression the track plays, a row of 2 to 16 boxes along the star's top //! (`drawProgressionEditor`) //! the star the main diagram, for the right hand: the scale's seven notes on a curve in thirds, and its //! seven chords round them (`StarLayout`) //! the key's window the scale's chords as the circle of fifths' chord wheel arranges them, each drawn as its //! guitar chord (`FifthsLayout`) //! the chooser the seven chords again, as buttons for the left hand's thumb (`ChooserLayout`) //! the twelve notes the octave's twelve pitch classes on a circle in order of pitch, the sounding ones joined and //! named as a chord (`ChromaticLayout`, `nameOfChord`) //! what sounds the notes sounding as a Lissajous figure, their chord's numeral over it and its function in //! the key under it - Tonic, Dominant (`drawChordCurve`, `drawChordNumeral`, `drawFunctionName`) //! the keyboard the scale's notes from the tonic to the tonic, laid out as a piano lays them (`drawKeyboard`) //! the options a panel along the left, opened from the top left and closed by a tap beside it //! (`buildOptions`): the scale, the progression track, the volumes and the display's choices //! //! The parts are laid out for the window's shape (`WindowParts`): on a phone held upright, the left column becomes a //! band across the top and the sounding box a strip under the star. The bottom right corner is left to the page's //! fullscreen button. //! //! The scale //! //! A scale is a tonic - A to G#, a sharp spelled as the tonic's letter raised - and a mode: the seven church modes and //! four more, harmonic and melodic minor, harmonic major, Phrygian dominant (`Scale`, `Mode`). Each degree is spelled //! with its own letter, so that a scale names each letter once - F# Ionian's seventh is E#, G# Ionian's F## - and //! carries a solfege syllable fixed to the letter, as French names notes. On each degree stands a triad, the degree and //! the notes a third and a fifth above it in the scale (`ScaleChord`); its quality - major, minor, diminished or //! augmented - is read from its semitones, and its numeral from its degree and quality: I, ii, vii. A progression may //! borrow a chord from outside the scale - III major where the key has iii minor - which is offered beside its root's //! own chord and, while held, raises or lowers the one note that differs (`alterationsForChord`). //! //! The star //! //! The notes stand on a curve in thirds - 1 3 5 7 2 4 6 - so that any three neighbours make a chord: 1 3 5 is I, 2 4 6 //! is ii. The curve is an ellipse whose bottom is cut off by a straight line, its height chosen so that the whole //! curve is seven equal steps long (`StarCurve`): every note is a step from the next, along the line or along the arc. //! As the star rests, 1, 3 and 5 stand on the line under the index, middle and ring fingers - the chosen chord's notes, //! drawn a fifth larger than the others, the tonic larger still. The white path joining the notes is the curve itself, //! arcs above and the line below, and halfway along each link sits a small copy of the note between its two ends in the //! scale - the 2 between 1 and 3 - so that a melody up the scale walks along the path (`NoteProxy`). //! //! Each chord stands at its third's place, a triplet of its three notes' shapes, its own in front (`ChordTriplet`): //! the chords of one side - the major side as the star rests - on a ring outside the curve, the others on a ring //! inside, the diminished chord outside. A chord's region is two fans from it to the arcs its notes span, root to third //! and third to fifth; every link of the curve is faced by one chord outside and one inside, so the white arc is where //! their regions meet and none cross (`drawChordShapes`). Lines run from a chord to its notes: an arrow to its root, a //! zigzag to its third, dashes to its fifth. The layout makes everything as large as the room allows at every one of //! the star's seven turns, no two targets nearer than their clearance (`StarLayout.settled`). //! //! The chosen chord's notes are outlined on the star by their part in it - root red, third yellow, fifth cyan - and its //! button in white (`drawChordOutlines`). Where the options say so, the star instead turns, in 0.04 seconds, to bring //! the chosen chord's notes into the row, so that the same three fingers play whichever chord is chosen, its chords //! trading sides so that the chosen one stands outside, below its notes (`aimStar`); while the star moves, it plays //! nothing. //! //! Playing //! //! Every finger plays what it touches and holds it until it lifts, following it as it slides (`readPointers`, //! `targetAt`): a note of the star, or its proxy; a chord of the star, at full strength; a chord of the chooser or of //! the key's window, at half strength, choosing it as well; a key of the keyboard; a note on the circle of twelve. The //! digits 1 to 7 play the degrees. A chord starts note by note - root, then third, then fifth, a strum's delay apart, //! 0.1 seconds unless the options say otherwise - so that its notes are heard (`holdChordDegrees`). A note sounds while //! anything holds it, as strongly as its strongest hold, and stops when the last lets go (`DegreeHolds`). The notes are //! Shepard tones, each sounding in every octave at once, so that notes differ in pitch class and not in height; two //! pedals - the chosen chord's root and the tonic - can be held low beneath everything (`updatePedals`). //! //! The progression track //! //! The track plays the progression in the editor's boxes, along the star's top: a row of 2 to 16, as chosen in the //! options, the empty ones passed over. A progression chosen in the options - a common one, or a song's, which also //! sets the song's key - is placed in the boxes (`placeChosenProgression`); a chord dragged from anywhere it plays - //! the star, the chooser, the key's window, a borrowed chord's button, another box - and dropped on a box replaces that //! box's chord, and the track plays it from its next turn (`carryChords`, `dropChord`). The track sends its chords //! travelling to their buttons on the chooser, one a bar at its tempo, a ghost of each button growing as it comes //! (`drawProgressionTrack`); the box playing is outlined in white. By default the track waits at each chord for the //! player to take it. The coming chord's notes are outlined on the star too, the outlines closing in on the notes as //! the chord arrives, and every outline pulses on the beat. With "play the chords", the track chooses each chord itself //! as it falls due, silently, the star following the song while the player plays its melody (`playProgressionChords`). //! //! The guitar chords //! //! Each chord of the key's window is drawn as a guitar chord chart, its fingering found by a search over every way to //! play the chord within four frets in standard tuning - the root lowest, all three notes, four fingers at most, a //! barre counting one - the cheapest by position, strings, fingers, stretch and open strings kept (`guitarChordOf`). //! The open-position chords come out as every chart has them. Each dot is in its note's color; a note sounding is //! ringed on every chart, and every other place on a chart where a sounding note could be played shows as a ring, so //! that a chord played elsewhere - Am7 on the keyboard - shows over the charts how a guitar would play it. //! //! The file //! //! The file reads from its vocabulary to its frame: the params, every color, size, speed, default and limit in one //! place (`params`); the scale - the degrees' colors, notes, chords and the circle of thirds; the pedals; shapes and //! their sizes; the chooser's curve and the star's; the star's layout; the window's parts, the chooser and the circle //! of twelve; guitar chords and the key's window; choosing a chord; the app's state; playing - holding and letting go //! of notes; reading the input and the options; the chord's curve; naming the chord; drawing; the outlines; and the //! frame, which runs them in turn. const std = @import("std"); // Names used often enough to be worth using bare: from the standard library, the engine (`z`) and its math // (`zm`). Each is the same declaration under a shorter name. const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator; const bufPrint = std.fmt.bufPrint; const splitScalar = std.mem.splitScalar; const asBytes = std.mem.asBytes; const indexOfScalar = std.mem.indexOfScalar; const eql = std.mem.eql; const endsWith = std.mem.endsWith; const startsWith = std.mem.startsWith; const z = @import("zimr"); const zm = @import("zm"); const Color = zm.Color; const Vec2 = zm.Vec2; const float = zm.float; const sinTurns = zm.sinTurns; const cosTurns = zm.cosTurns; const length = zm.length; const assert = zm.assert; const clamp = zm.clamp; const smoothstep = zm.smoothstep; const exp = zm.exp; const exp2 = zm.exp2; const log2 = zm.log2; const sqrt = zm.sqrt; const inf = zm.inf; const maxInt = zm.maxInt; const gcd = zm.gcd; const pi = zm.pi; const float64 = zm.float64; const splat2 = zm.splat2; /// The font every text is drawn in: Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono, made for legibility, its letters distinct at small /// sizes - embedded in the app. const atkinson_mono_ttf = @embedFile("atkinson_mono_ttf"); // ---- The params ---- /// The app's tunable values in one place: every color, size, speed, default and limit the code reads and never /// changes, grouped by topic. Each is read where it is needed - `params.colors.background` - and never passed. const params = struct { /// The colors: the window's, the text's and the marks', each degree's own, and the outlines'. const colors = struct { /// The window's background: a near-black, blue-grey, against which the degrees' colors read clearly. const background: Color = .{ .r = 16, .g = 17, .b = 22, .a = 255 }; /// Text and white marks: a soft white. const text: Color = .{ .r = 235, .g = 235, .b = 240, .a = 255 }; /// Text that matters less, and a chart's fret number: a mid grey. const dim_text: Color = .{ .r = 150, .g = 156, .b = 170, .a = 255 }; /// The thin lines of the boxes round the diagrams and the circle of twelve: a dark grey. const note_path: Color = .{ .r = 70, .g = 74, .b = 90, .a = 255 }; /// The notes' outlines and the circle of thirds' path: a white a little softer than the text's. const outline: Color = .{ .r = 225, .g = 228, .b = 236, .a = 255 }; /// A chosen chord's note's own outline: black, inside its colored one. const chosen_note_outline: Color = .{ .r = 0, .g = 0, .b = 0, .a = 255 }; /// Text on a lit note or chord, which is filled with its full color: dark, since some of the colors are light. const lit_text: Color = .{ .r = 16, .g = 17, .b = 22, .a = 255 }; /// Each degree's color, as a rainbow keyboard colors its white keys from C: red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, /// blue, violet. A note is filled with its color, dimmed until it sounds; a chord takes its root's color. const degrees = [7]Color{ .rgbHex(0xF52A2A), .rgbHex(0xFFA514), .rgbHex(0xFFF200), .rgbHex(0x18E018), .rgbHex(0x18E6F0), .rgbHex(0x1464FF), .rgbHex(0xA83CF0), }; /// The boxes round the left hand's diagrams (`window.left_diagram_box_inset`): the star's note path's color, /// quiet on the background. const left_diagram_box: Color = note_path; /// A chord's outline: black, so that the chords - small among the notes - stand apart from them. const chord_outline: Color = .{ .r = 0, .g = 0, .b = 0, .a = 255 }; /// The colors the outlines give a note by its part in a chord: its root red, its third yellow, its fifth cyan - /// the colors of the chord's own lines to its notes (`drawChordLine`): the arrow, the zigzag, the dashes. const role_outlines = [3]Color{ .{ .r = 235, .g = 52, .b = 52, .a = 255 }, .{ .r = 250, .g = 222, .b = 40, .a = 255 }, .{ .r = 0, .g = 222, .b = 236, .a = 255 }, }; /// A black key of the keyboard: a little lighter than the background, so that it reads as a key against it. const black_key: Color = .{ .r = 0, .g = 0, .b = 0, .a = 255 }; /// A white key the scale does not use: grey, a little lighter than the boxes' lines. const unused_white_key: Color = .{ .r = 92, .g = 96, .b = 108, .a = 255 }; /// The light gray of a chart's strings and frets. const guitar_line: Color = .{ .r = 196, .g = 200, .b = 210, .a = 255 }; }; /// How far toward the background a color is drawn while what it fills is silent. const dimming = struct { /// How far toward the background a color is drawn while its note or chord is silent: lit, it is drawn whole. const resting: f32 = 0.45; /// How far toward the background a chord's fans are drawn (`drawChordShapes`): faint while the chord is /// silent, a little less faint while it sounds. const Fan = struct { /// While the chord is silent. resting: f32, /// While it sounds. lit: f32, }; /// The fan to the arc from the root to the third is the more opaque of a chord's two: the third is what makes a /// chord major or minor. const root_third_fan: Fan = .{ .resting = 0.8, .lit = 0.6 }; /// The fan to the arc from the third to the fifth, fainter. const third_fifth_fan: Fan = .{ .resting = 0.9, .lit = 0.76 }; }; /// The options' values as the app starts (`initState`), each named after the field it starts. const defaults = struct { /// How hard the chord held on the chooser strikes its notes, by default, as a share of the other notes' /// strength (`State.chooser_chord_volume`, set in the options): 0.3 of it, so that the left thumb's chord /// sounds well beneath what the right hand plays (`HoldLayer.thumb`). const chooser_chord_volume: f32 = 0.3; /// A pedal's loudness by default, as its voice's volume (`Pedal.volume`, set in the options): 0, silent - the /// pedals sound only once their sliders are raised. const pedal_volume: f32 = 0; /// The options' first choice of how many boxes, an index into `progression.box_counts`: 4. const progression_box_count_choice: i32 = 2; /// The progression's tempo, in beats a minute (`State.progression_beats_per_minute`, set in the options). const progression_beats_per_minute: f32 = 90; /// The delay between a chord's notes as it starts (`State.chord_strum_seconds`, set in the options): 0.1 /// seconds, quick enough to be one chord, slow enough to hear its notes come in. const chord_strum_seconds: f32 = 0.1; }; /// Playing: how hard a note is struck, how far a finger moves before it changes what it plays or carries a chord, /// and the keys that play the degrees. const playing = struct { /// How hard every note is struck: half the instrument's full level, so that a chord of three stays clear of /// clipping. const note_velocity: f32 = 0.5; /// The keys that play each degree while held: the top row's digits and the keypad's. const digit_keys = [7]z.KeyboardKey{ .one, .two, .three, .four, .five, .six, .seven }; /// The keypad's digits, which play the degrees as the top row's do (`digit_keys`). const keypad_keys = [7]z.KeyboardKey{ .kp_1, .kp_2, .kp_3, .kp_4, .kp_5, .kp_6, .kp_7 }; /// How far a pointer must move from where it took its target before it takes another: 6 pixels. Every point of /// the star, the chooser, the key's window and the circle belongs to its nearest target, so boundaries run /// everywhere, and a finger resting near one moves a pixel or two back and forth between touch events - each /// time it crossed, the note it held was let go and the next one struck, many times a second, heard as crackle. /// A finger sliding on moves far more than this, and changes target as soon as it crosses; one resting keeps /// what it holds. const target_switch_distance: f32 = 6; /// How far a finger carrying a chord goes from where it came down before the chord is shown following it, and /// before a box under it takes the chord when it lifts: 12 pixels - a tap's wobble does not carry a chord /// anywhere. const chord_drag_start_distance: f32 = 12; }; /// The pedals' sound (`generatePedal`). const pedal = struct { /// The pedals: notes held low beneath everything while their checkboxes at the top are ticked, as an organist /// holds notes with the feet - one on the chosen chord's root, following the left hand, the other on the /// scale's tonic, unchanging. Each is a Shepard tone like the notes the hands play, but lower: the same pitch /// class sounding in every octave at once under a bell of loudness, the bell centred two octaves down - at /// 100 Hz rather than the instrument's 400. It keeps the notes' character, a pitch class with no height of its /// own, and sits beneath them. Each plays as a voice of its own (`generatePedal`), beside the instrument's /// notes. const bell_centre_hz: f64 = 100; /// The bell's width, its partials and their reach: as the Shepard instrument's (`z.mixer.shepard_*`) - one /// octave's standard deviation, ten partials an octave apart, five octaves either side of the centre. const bell_width_octaves: f64 = 1; /// Ten partials, an octave apart. const partial_count: usize = 10; /// The partials' reach: five octaves either side of the bell's centre. const reach_octaves: f64 = 5; /// How long a pedal takes to rise from silence to full: 30 ms, so that it starts without a click. const attack_seconds: f32 = 0.03; }; /// The notes' and chords' sizes, in size units, and the shares of them drawn (`ShapedSize`). const sizes = struct { /// How far apart the three shapes of a chord's triplet stand on the star, as a share of a shape's width: a /// third, so that each hides two thirds of the one behind it (`ChordTriplet`). const chord_triplet_step_share: f32 = 1.0 / 3.0; /// A note's size: two units. const note_size_in_units: f32 = 2; /// The chosen chord's three notes - its root, third and fifth, at the places of 1, 3 and 5 under the right /// hand - are its heroes, drawn a fifth larger than the others. const hero_note_size_in_units: f32 = 2.4; /// The tonic beside the other notes, in every diagram - the star, the chooser, the key's window, the circle of /// the twelve: 30% larger, the scale's home found at a glance. const tonic_size_share: f32 = 1.3; /// How large a note is drawn beside the room the star's layout keeps for it (`StarLayout.noteHalfSize`): 95%, /// and the tonic 90%. const note_drawn_share: f32 = 0.95; /// The tonic's, a little smaller still, as it is the larger. const tonic_drawn_share: f32 = 0.9; /// A chord's size: one unit. const chord_size_in_units: f32 = 1; /// The scale's two main chords', a quarter larger. const main_chord_size_in_units: f32 = 1.25; /// The diminished chord's, a quarter smaller. const diminished_chord_size_in_units: f32 = 0.75; /// The largest of the chords' sizes: what the chooser's spacing must allow for. const largest_chord_size_in_units: f32 = main_chord_size_in_units; }; /// The star's path and its turning (`drawNotePath`, `StarTransition`). const star = struct { /// The straight pieces each link of the star's curve is drawn in - the white path (`drawNotePath`) and the /// chords' fans' edges along it (`drawChordFan`), the same pieces, so that a fan meets the path exactly. const curve_pieces_per_link: usize = 24; /// How long the star takes to turn to a newly chosen chord, its chords trading sides with it: 0.04 seconds, /// under three frames at 60 a second - quick enough to follow the hand, slow enough to be seen moving. const transition_duration_seconds: f32 = 0.04; /// The circle of thirds' thickness beside the notes' outlines: 1.4 times. const note_path_thickness_share: f32 = 1.4; }; /// The small copies of the notes halfway along the star's links (`NoteProxy`). const note_proxy = struct { /// How much of the room between a proxy and the notes either side of it the proxy takes for touches: three /// quarters; the rest, by the notes' edges, stays theirs. const room_share: f32 = 0.75; /// A proxy's size beside its note's: 22%. const size_share: f32 = 0.22; /// How far a touch reaches a proxy: within 1.8 times its half-size - more than its little size, so that a /// finger sliding along the link meets it, and less than halfway to the notes on either side. const reach: f32 = 1.8; /// The opacity of a proxy's fill, out of 255: faint beside the notes. const alpha: u8 = 150; }; /// The window's parts: their shares of it and the room kept between and inside them (`WindowParts`). const window = struct { /// The room left between the keyboard's end and the fullscreen button, beyond the margin. const keyboard_gap_before_button: f32 = 16; /// The left hand's share of the window: its column - or its band, on a screen held upright - a quarter, leaving /// the star, where the right hand plays, the rest. The chooser's buttons are as large as its width allows: at a /// phone's proportions, 900 by 415, their size unit is 17.3 at a share of 0.21, 20.6 at this one - a fifth /// larger, room for their names - and no larger beyond it, the column's height then the limit. const chooser_share: f32 = 0.252; /// The key's window on the circle of fifths (`drawFifths`): its share of the left hand's column, at the top - /// 65%, room for its guitar chords - the chooser the rest below, 35%, its curve squished flatter to fit /// (`ChooserLayout.vertical_squish`). const fifths_share: f32 = 0.65; /// The circle of the twelve notes, at the top right: the side of its square as a share of the window's width. const chromatic_share: f32 = 0.2; /// The sounding box's height on a window held upright, as a share of the content's width: 30%. const upright_sounding_share: f32 = 0.3; /// The space between the left hand's column and the star, as a share of the content's width: 4%. const star_gap_share: f32 = 0.04; /// The space the header's window keeps after its text: its own padding, and a little more. const header_padding: f32 = 16; /// How far inside its part each of the left hand's diagrams is drawn: its box 3 pixels in - so that the key's /// window's and the chooser's, one above the other, do not touch - and its buttons 5 pixels in, clear of the /// box. Measured at a phone's proportions, 900 by 415, both diagrams then fit a size unit of 19.3, the two in /// balance with half the column's height each; 8 pixels in, 18.5. const left_diagram_box_inset: f32 = 3; /// The room kept inside each box, between its line and what it holds, in pixels. const left_diagram_padding: f32 = 5; /// How much of the circle's side the star stops short of the content's right edge: all of it - the star's room /// ends where the circle's square begins. Its top right corner holds the 7 and its chord now that the curve no /// longer pulls the 7 down beside the row (`warpAt`), and the star, fitted for every turn, would reach into the /// circle there. const star_under_chromatic_share: f32 = 1.0; /// A borrowed chord's button's size, as a share of its root's chord's. const borrowed_button_share: f32 = 0.6; /// The options panel's width, as a share of the window's - 70% - and the least it is: 460 pixels, for its /// labels. const options_panel_share: f32 = 0.7; /// The least the panel is: 460 pixels, room for its labels. const options_panel_least_width: f32 = 460; }; /// The keyboard's keys (`drawKeyboard`). const keyboard = struct { /// A black key's width and height beside a white key's: 60% of each. const black_key_width_share: f32 = 0.6; const black_key_height_share: f32 = 0.6; /// How far a sounding key rises above the keyboard, as a share of its height: 30%. const sounding_key_rise_share: f32 = 0.3; }; /// The outlines of the chosen chord's notes and of the coming chord's (`drawChordOutlines`). const outline = struct { /// The outlines' sizes, as shares of the note's half-size: the gap between a note and its outline; the chosen /// chord's outline's thickness, and the coming chord's, thinner; and how far out the coming chord's outline /// starts, closing in on its note as the chord travels to its button. const gap_share: f32 = 0.18; /// The chosen chord's outlines' thickness. const chosen_share: f32 = 0.26; /// The coming chord's, thinner. const coming_share: f32 = 0.07; /// How far out the coming chord's outline starts, closing in on its note as the chord comes. const coming_reach_share: f32 = 0.9; /// The coming chord's button's outline beside its notes': twice as thick, and setting out five times as far. const coming_button_thickness_factor: f32 = 2; const coming_button_reach_factor: f32 = 5; /// The share of a bar the coming chord's outlines show for, on every view - the star's notes and button, the /// keyboard's keys, the circle's notes: its second half, the outlines appearing at its middle and closing in by /// its end, as the chord arrives. const coming_shown_share: f32 = 0.5; }; /// The progression track and its editor (`advanceProgression`, `drawProgressionEditor`). const progression = struct { /// The beats each chord of a progression lasts: a bar of four. const beats_per_chord: f64 = 4; /// How many boxes the editor shows, as the options offer them - the progressions' lengths and the bars' usual /// groupings - and their labels there. const box_counts = [_]u8{ 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16 }; const box_count_labels = [_][]const u8{ "2 boxes", "3 boxes", "4 boxes", "6 boxes", "8 boxes", "12 boxes", "16 boxes", }; /// How far short of its arrival the track holds a chord awaited, following the player (`advanceProgression`): a /// millionth of a beat - so the chord is still the one on its way, drawn at its button, not yet the one to /// play. const hold_beats: f64 = 1e-6; /// How fast the chord the track waits for pulses, and how much it grows (`waitingScale`): three times a /// second - quicker than the beat, so that it reads as a call to play it rather than as the music's pulse - up /// to a fifth larger. const waiting_pulses_per_second: f32 = 3; const waiting_pulse_growth: f32 = 0.2; /// The playhead's width, in pixels (`drawProgressionEditor`). const playhead_width: f32 = 2; }; /// The guitar chords: the tuning, the frets searched and the charts (`guitarChordOf`, `drawGuitarChord`). const guitar = struct { /// The guitar's six strings in standard tuning, the lowest first - E A D G B E - as MIDI keys, E2 to E4. const string_keys = [6]u8{ 40, 45, 50, 55, 59, 64 }; /// The frets a chord's fingering spans at most: four, the hand's reach - a window from its lowest fret pressed. const window_frets: u8 = 4; /// The highest fret a fingering's window starts at: the 12th, an octave up the neck. const highest_window: u8 = 12; /// How much larger a chart's own notes are drawn than a plain dot: 30%, whole, even where they overlap. const chart_note_scale: f32 = 1.3; }; /// The dots moving along the lines between pitch neighbours in the left hand's column (`drawColumnStar`). const column_dots = struct { /// The dots' spacing in the left hand's column, in the chooser's size units: the chooser's and the key's /// window's steps in pitch, at the size of their buttons. const spacing_units: f32 = 0.5; /// How many times a second the dots of a line between pitch neighbours move on by one dot's spacing. const dots_per_second: f32 = 3; /// How far toward the background a column star's dots are drawn while neither of their notes sounds: 20%. const resting_dimming: f32 = 0.2; }; /// What sounds: its figure's turning and the band naming its function (`drawChordCurve`). const sounding = struct { /// How fast a three-note curve turns, in turns a second: slow enough to follow its shape as it turns. const curve_turns_per_second: f32 = 0.08; /// The sounding box's bottom band, where the function's name is written under the figure, as a share of its /// height: 20%. const function_name_band_share: f32 = 0.2; }; /// How many of each the state and the drawing have room for. const limits = struct { /// The room for one progression's label in the options' list: its name, its numbers and its chords' names in /// the key. const progression_label_capacity: usize = 96; /// The room one mode's label takes in the header's list (`writeModeLabels`): a line of its name and /// alterations, and a line of seven chord names of at most four bytes each - a letter, an accidental and a /// degree sign of two. const mode_label_capacity: usize = 96;
